# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 1

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 1 — The Two Ways (Introduction)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 7

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.2: Negative Golden Rule phrasing

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "all things whatsoever you do not wish to happen to you, do not do to another" |
| LOGOS | "whatever you do not wish to be done to you, do not do to another" |
| PNEUMA | "whatever you would not want done to you, do not do to anyone else" |

**Issue:** Degree of literalness vs. naturalness in the negative Golden Rule. EMET preserves the "all things whatsoever" (πάντα δὲ ὅσα) quantifier; LOGOS and PNEUMA smooth it out.
**Ruling:** LOGOS phrasing adopted. The quantifier is redundant in English and the LOGOS form best balances accuracy and readability.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.3: "merit" vs. "credit"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "what credit is it" |
| LOGOS | "what merit is there" |
| PNEUMA | "what's so impressive about" |

**Issue:** The Greek χάρις (charis) here means "what grace/favor" — i.e., what moral credit before God. EMET's "credit" and LOGOS's "merit" are both viable; PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the theological resonance.
**Ruling:** EMET's "credit" adopted. Matches the Lukan parallel (Luke 6:32–34) and preserves the theological register.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: "pagans" vs. "Gentiles"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "Gentiles" |
| LOGOS | "Gentiles" |
| PNEUMA | "pagans" |

**Issue:** ἔθνη in a Jewish-Christian document carries the covenantal distinction of Jew vs. non-Jew, not merely the religious distinction of Christian vs. pagan.
**Ruling:** "Gentiles" retained. The Didache community likely included Jewish Christians for whom this distinction was meaningful.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.4: τέλειος — "perfect" vs. "complete"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "you will be perfect" |
| LOGOS | "you will be complete" |
| PNEUMA | "that's how you reach wholeness" |

**Issue:** τέλειος can mean perfect, mature, complete, or whole. "Perfect" risks a moralistic/impossible standard; "complete" suggests integrated maturity.
**Ruling:** "Complete" adopted. Better conveys the Didache's practical ethics without implying sinless perfection.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.4: Structure of the "give your tunic" passage

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | Preserves "for you are not even able to do so" as a separate clause |
| LOGOS | Same structure |
| PNEUMA | "You can't get it back anyway" — paraphrase |

**Issue:** PNEUMA's colloquial rendering loses the understated force of the Greek's frank parenthetical.
**Ruling:** Formal structure retained. The matter-of-fact acknowledgment of powerlessness is theologically and socially significant.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.5: "cast into prison" vs. "thrown into prison"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "being put in prison" |
| LOGOS | "thrown into prison" |
| PNEUMA | "end up thrown in prison" |

**Issue:** Minor stylistic difference; the Greek βληθήσεται (will be cast/thrown) is a future passive.
**Ruling:** "Cast into prison" adopted in final. Matches the eschatological register of divine judgment implicit in the passage.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.6: ἱδρωσάτω — rendering the sweat image

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "Let your alms sweat in your hands" |
| LOGOS | "Let your alms sweat in your hands" |
| PNEUMA | "Let your gift sweat in your hands" |

**Issue:** ἐλεημοσύνη = almsgiving/charity (a technical term in Jewish/Christian ethics), not merely "gift."
**Ruling:** "Alms" retained. The term carries the weight of Jewish practice of tzedakah and should not be softened to a generic "gift."
